Deep research agents are often trained on expensive, environment-grounded tool-
use trajectories that require repeated retrieval, document inspection, and report
evaluation. We introduce Deep Research Pretraining (DRP), an offline framework
that derives predictive-navigation supervision from naturally occurring evidence
structures. Given a citation-bearing or hyperlinked passage, DRP constructs a
proxy research objective, recovers linked evidence and graph-related alternatives,
and converts them into search–open–write trajectories. This teaches models what
to search for, which documents to inspect, and how to synthesize evidence, with-
out a live retrieval environment or executed policy rollout. We instantiate DRP
on scholarly citation graphs (DRP-Paper) and Wikipedia hyperlinks (DRP-Web),
continually pretrain separate Qwen3-14B-Base models on 1B tokens, and fine-
tune them on

with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base used for scale analysis. Unless stated otherwise, each DRP corpus uses

1B-token CPT budget and downstream SFT setting. In Figure 6(a), DRP-Web gains 5.3 points over
Base, compared with 0.8 for Raw-Web; DRP-Paper gains 5.0 points, whereas Raw-Paper decreases
by 4.8. The corresponding direct DRP–Raw advantages are 4.5 and 9.8 points, with both paired-
bootstrap intervals above zero (Figure 6(b)). Thus, source-matched domain exposure is not sufficient
to account for the predictive-navigation gain.

evidence.excerpt:
The raw-document controls establish an advantage for structured DRP over raw CPT, but do
not isolate whether the constructed observations must be relevant to the model's decisions. We
therefore perform a controlled ablation in our canonical DRP-Web analysis setting. Evidence-
Mismatched DRP-Web preserves the proxy queries, synthetic reasoning, action schedule, tool-call
syntax, response-length distribution, and training budget of aligned DRP-Web, but replaces graph-
derived search and open observations with random in-domain evidence. Aligned DRP-Web gains
5.3 points over Base, while evidence-mismatched DRP-Web gains only 1.1; their direct difference is
4.2 points with its 95% bootstrap interval above zero (Figure 7). Breaking query–observation–action
alignment therefore removes most of the gain even though the agent-like surface form is preserved.

We test whether specializing CPT toward DRP harms general capabilities under a fixed 2B-token
budget starting from Qwen3-14B-Base. The control uses 2B tokens of general midtraining data from
the fully open OLMo 3 training flow (Team OLMo et al., 2025); the mixed condition replaces half of
that budget with 1B DRP-Web tokens. Our 14-benchmark suite spans commonsense reasoning (e.g.,
ARC), mathematical reasoning (GSM8K), knowledge (MMLU-Redux), and reading comprehension
(DROP); Appendix C.4 provides the complete suite, citations, and per-benchmark results. Table 4
shows that the aggregate score changes from 73.1 to 73.4. After matched1/16DR-Tulu SFT, the
mixed checkpoint improves the score from 33.1 to 36.8 (+3.7 points). Thus, replacing half of the
general CPT budget with DRP-Web preserves aggregate general capability in this evaluation while
improving downstream agent initialization.

Training and supervising research agents.WebGPT and ReAct establish browser-assisted ques-
tion answering and the interleaving of language-model reasoning with external actions (Nakano
et al., 2021; Yao et al., 2023). Recent deep-research systems train these behaviors through search-
environment RL, teacher-generated trajectories, synthetic tasks, and report-level rubrics (Jin et al.,
2025; Zheng et al., 2025; Shao et al., 2025; Xie et al., 2026). ARPO further adapts policy optimiza-
tion to multi-turn tool-use exploration (Dong et al., 2026). ZeroSearch and OpenResearcher reduce
the cost of this supervision through simulated retrieval or a local search-and-browse environment
(Sun et al., 2025; Li et al., 2026). These approaches improve the downstream post-training process

resample question IDs with replacement, preserving the pairing between systems, recompute the
mean score difference for each bootstrap replicate, and report the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. This
paired bootstrap captures uncertainty over the evaluated questions while holding the trained check-
points fixed. It is therefore complementary to, rather than interchangeable with, the subset-levelt
intervals above. We use 10,000 bootstrap replicates with random seed 42.

F ADDITIONALLIMITATIONS
The current experiments use English downstream trajectories and one released trajectory source. The
primary DRB evaluation has 50 English questions, making paired evaluation and transparent uncer-
tainty reporting especially important. The five-run design measures downstream subset sensitivity
but does not estimate the full interaction among subset sampling, training randomness, decoding
randomness, and judge variation. Most construction ablations use one fixed SFT subset and paired
question-level bootstrap intervals. Finally, DRP's gain attenuates with more downstream SFT data.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The transfer evaluations report accuracy and coverage using a separate Qwen3-30B judge on held-out WebWalkerQA, SimpleQA and ResearchQA, outside the DRB RACE evaluator.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: GPT-5.5 RACE scoring on DeepResearch Bench, plus a separate Qwen3-30B judge scoring accuracy and coverage on the transfer benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Masked causal language modeling loss on agent tokens from offline-reconstructed trajectories, with further optimization by GPT-5 trajectory SFT.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported claims regarding trajectory sample efficiency gains, persistence through RL, and the necessity of evidence alignment are tightly supported by matched baselines and ablation experiments.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluations are rigorously structured across multiple subsets with paired statistical tests (Student-t over subsets, paired bootstraps over items). Results demonstrate consistent sample-efficiency gains across DeepResearch Bench, downstream agentic RL, and out-of-domain benchmarks like ResearchQA, WebWalkerQA, and SimpleQA, accompanied by general-capability checks and n-gram contamination analyses.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations on WebWalkerQA, SimpleQA, and ResearchQA measure factual answer accuracy and coverage independently of the GPT-5.5 RACE judge, corroborating the sample-efficiency gains.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: GPT-5.5 RACE rubric scoring on DeepResearch Bench, as well as objective QA accuracy and coverage metrics on WebWalkerQA, SimpleQA, and ResearchQA evaluated by an independent local judge.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Masked causal language modeling loss on Qwen3.6-35B-generated rationales and action sequences derived offline from document graphs, followed by SFT on GPT-5 trajectory fractions.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly acknowledge the modest benchmark size (50 DRB questions), focus on English-only corpora and single expert trajectory sources, lack of full variance estimation across decoding/judge interactions, and the attenuation of gains under full downstream SFT budgets.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing graph extraction, proxy objective inference, interleaved candidate synthesis, and masked causal language model pretraining across both academic papers (DRP-Paper) and web text (DRP-Web). Clear operational controls isolate evidence alignment, raw domain exposure, trajectory topologies, protocol rendering, and observation loss masking.
primary.quality_rationale: The study offers a solid, well-controlled experimental validation of offline graph-derived pretraining for research agents, supported by rigorous paired statistics, clear negative controls, and comprehensive ablation studies.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces Deep Research Pretraining (DRP), an offline framework that converts naturally occurring evidence graphs (citation networks and web hyperlinks) into rollout-free predictive navigation trajectories for continual pretraining, improving downstream agent SFT sample efficiency.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study offers a solid, well-controlled experimental validation of offline graph-derived pretraining for research agents, supported by rigorous paired statistics, clear negative controls, and comprehensive ablation studies.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly acknowledge the modest benchmark size (50 DRB questions), focus on English-only corpora and single expert trajectory sources, lack of full variance estimation across decoding/judge interactions, and the attenuation of gains under full downstream SFT budgets.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
